items.title: Sign S3-compatible object storage (Hetzner, R2, B2, MinIO), not only AWS

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
## Problem

The gateway already signs AWS requests with SigV4 (`apps/gateway/src/gateway/finalizers/aws_sigv4.rs`), but only for the compiled-in `aws` provider whose host rules match `.amazonaws.com` / `.api.aws`. A non-AWS S3-compatible endpoint (Hetzner Object Storage, Cloudflare R2, Backblaze B2, MinIO) can't be signed, for two reasons:

1. Nothing routes a non-AWS host to the SigV4 finalizer.
2. `parse_service_region("nbg1.your-objectstorage.com")` returns `("unknown", ...)`, so the credential scope is wrong and S3 rejects the request.

A `generic` secret doesn't help: it injects a static header, but S3 auth is a computed per-request signature over the request, not a fixed token.

Concretely: I run an archive/search tool (pond) against a Hetzner bucket and want the bucket keys to live in the OneCLI vault instead of on the sandbox machine, with the gateway signing on the wire so the agent never holds them.

## Proposal

Add an `aws` secret type that carries the IAM keys (`{ accessKeyId, secretAccessKey, sessionToken? }`) plus `{ region, service? }` (service defaults to `s3`). The gateway emits the existing internal `x-onecli-aws-*` headers plus an explicit service, and the SigV4 finalizer signs any host when those headers are present. AWS hosts keep working unchanged, since they still parse service/region from the hostname.

## Context

Discussed on the 2026-07-07 call with @johnnyfish and @guyb1, who invited a PR. Related but separate from #417 (credential use beyond HTTP injection). Draft PR ready to open.

items.title: Credential use beyond HTTP injection: local signing, SSH, and other non-HTTP flows

labels.name: area/gateway
labels.description: Proxy, routing, TLS, DNS, credential injection

items.body:
## Context

Discussed on a call with @johnnyfish and @guyb1 on 2026-07-07; opening this so it isn't lost.

I run OneCLI self-hosted as the credential layer for sandboxed agents (NanoClaw). The HTTPS injection model works well for vendor API keys: sentinel value on disk, real credential injected at the gateway, agent never holds a secret. The problem is everything that isn't an outbound HTTPS request. For those flows the current answer is "put the key on the machine", which defeats the reason OneCLI exists.

## Concrete cases I've hit

1. **Local signing/decryption (sops/age).** My deploy secrets are sops-encrypted in the repo; `helm apply` decrypts them for a single invocation via an age key. The key is used for local crypto - there is no HTTP request to inject into - so today the private key must sit on the agent's filesystem.
2. **SSH.** A sysadmin-style agent that SSHes into other machines to check logs or restart services. SSH keys can't be injected by the gateway (different protocol), so again: key on disk.
3. **Databases / other TCP.** Postgres credentials don't traverse HTTPS. No mechanism today.

## Prior art: the 1Password SSH agent

1Password solved exactly this shape for SSH: their agent speaks the standard SSH agent protocol (`SSH_AUTH_SOCK` / `IdentityAgent`), the private key never leaves the 1Password app, and every signing request from a client requires explicit user authorization (touch ID / system auth). The client gets a signature, never the key. That's the model I use locally today - and the reason I can't yet move those workflows onto remote sandboxes.

## Proposed direction

An `oc`-style command-line invocation surface backed by the vault, where the vault performs the operation instead of releasing the key:

- **SSH**: OneCLI ships/exposes an SSH agent socket backed by the vault - the sandbox's `ssh` client asks the agent for signatures, OneCLI applies policy/approval, key never lands on the machine. The agent-protocol seam means zero changes to ssh itself.
- **Signing/decrypt operations** (`oc exec -- <cmd>` or similar): for sops/age-class flows, the decrypt/sign step talks to the OneCLI server, optionally gated by the existing approval flow (the same approve/reject cards NanoClaw already surfaces).
- **Policy**: per-agent assignment, rules, and approval should apply to these operations exactly like HTTP injections - and ideally policy could consider invocation context (which process/agent invoked it), though we agreed on the call that's a hard problem.

## Honest scope caveat

For the sops case specifically: if the operation decrypts secrets on the agent's machine, a determined agent can still reach the plaintext (memory, piped output). So the realistic protection tiers are:

- **Tier 1 (achievable):** the *key* never lands on disk and every use is policy-gated, auditable, revocable - even if that invocation's output is exposed.
- **Tier 2 (harder):** the operation runs vault-side and only the effect is returned (true signing service). Right for SSH auth and signatures; not always possible for decrypt-and-use flows.

Tier 1 alone would already be a big step - standing keys on sandbox filesystems are the thing I most want to eliminate.

## Non-solution to rule out

SSH-over-HTTP-proxy was floated on the call: an SSH connection through the gateway is an opaque CONNECT tunnel - there's nothing for the gateway to inspect or inject into - so it doesn't help here.

## Why this matters

Agents on remote/ephemeral sandboxes are exactly where OneCLI shines, and exactly where these flows (deploy, SSH, DB) show up. Today I can cover ~everything HTTPS and nothing else; this gap decides whether OneCLI can be the *single* credential layer for an agent fleet.

Related, will file separately: SigV4 re-signing currently activates only for `.amazonaws.com` hosts, so S3-compatible stores (Hetzner, R2, B2, MinIO) can't use it - I have a small patch and will open a PR as discussed.

items.title: feat: Google Service Account secret type (JWT → Bearer token injection)

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
## Summary

Add a `google_service_account` secret type that lets agents call Google APIs (Drive, Sheets, etc.) authenticated as a GCP service account — without the SA private key ever entering the agent's environment.

The gateway holds the SA JSON key in the vault, signs a short-lived JWT (RS256), exchanges it at `oauth2.googleapis.com/token`, caches the access token, and injects it as a Bearer header into matching requests. This is the same pattern the GitHub App integration already uses (private key → signed JWT → short-lived token → header injection).

## Motivation / use case

Multi-agent setups where different agents need access to *different* Google Drive data. Example: an HR agent and a Dev agent, each assigned (via selective secret mode) a different service account that is a member of only its department's shared drive. Isolation is enforced by Google-side permissions + per-agent secret grants — a compromised agent cannot reach the other department's data, and cannot exfiltrate the key because only the resolved short-lived token ever crosses the gateway.

The existing OAuth "apps" connectors cover human-account flows, and Vertex AI covers `cloud-platform` scope on aiplatform hosts, but there is currently no way to use a plain service account against general Google APIs.

## Design decisions (feedback welcome)

- **Secret, not App.** SA keys are bring-your-own credentials with a user-configurable host pattern, which matches the Secret abstraction
  (host/path matching + injection). Apps are provider integrations with lifecycle management. Happy to discuss if you'd prefer this as an app  provider instead.
- **Token resolution in the connect phase**, mirroring the existing OpenAI OAuth refresh (`connect.rs`), keeping `build_injections()` synchronous.
- **JWT claims omit `sub`.** `sub` is only meaningful for domain-wide delegation; without DWD it can cause `invalid_grant`. (The Vertex AI path
  keeps `sub` — unchanged.) Shared JWT-exchange logic could be factored out of `refresh_via_service_account()` with `scope`/`sub` parameterized.
- **Default hostPattern `www.googleapis.com`** (not `*.googleapis.com`), to avoid matching the token endpoint and colliding with Vertex AI hosts. An
  explicit guard also skips injection for `oauth2.googleapis.com` even if a user broadens the pattern.
- **In-memory token cache** (~50 min TTL, 10 min safety margin), keyed by `secret_id + hash(secret value)` so key rotation invalidates immediately.
  No DB write-back. Note: on the Cloud edition this cache is Redis, meaning short-lived access tokens would transit the shared cache — flagging for review.
- **Scope hardcoded to `drive.readonly` for MVP**, surfaced in the UI.
  Configurable scopes (via secret metadata) planned as a follow-up.
- **Metadata stores only `client_email` / `project_id`** — never the private
  key. Tests assert the key does not leak into metadata or error messages.

## Status

Implemented in my fork (yosukekmt/onecli), including validation/service layer, dialog UI with JSON key upload + parsed preview, gateway resolution with the cache behavior above, and unit tests (validation, service layer, and token-resolution cache hit/miss/expiry/rotation via an injected fetcher).

I'd like to submit this as a PR for this.

items.title: GitHub App (BYOC): Reconnect navigates to existing installation page instead of triggering fresh auth flow

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
## Problem

When a GitHub App is already installed on an org and connected in OneCLI, clicking **Connect** in the OneCLI web UI navigates the browser to the existing installation settings page (`https://github.com/organizations/<org>/settings/installations/<installation-id>`) instead of triggering the OAuth install flow. OneCLI still shows the connection as incomplete. There is no error message — the browser just lands on the GitHub settings page and the user has no indication of what to do.

## Root cause

The OAuth-during-installation flow only fires on a *fresh* install. When the app is already installed on the org, GitHub skips the install step and opens the existing installation management page instead of completing the OAuth callback to OneCLI.

## Common triggers

- Changing the **App Slug** in OneCLI after renaming the GitHub App
- Adding a new **permission scope** to the GitHub App (which requires a re-auth to pick up the new scope)

Both cases require a fresh install to complete, but the current Reconnect flow has no way to detect this or guide the user through it.

## Workaround

1. Go to the installation settings page GitHub opened — Danger zone — **Uninstall**.
2. Return to OneCLI and click **Connect** — this triggers a fresh install + OAuth flow through the callback URL.

## Suggested improvement

OneCLI already knows the existing installation ID (it navigates there directly), so it can detect this case. Two sub-cases worth handling differently:

- **Slug/name change or general reconnect**: prompt the user — *"This app is already installed. To re-authorize, uninstall it first — [Open installation settings]."*
- **New permissions pending review**: GitHub shows a "review new permissions" prompt on the installation page. This doesn't require a full uninstall — OneCLI could surface a direct link to that review page rather than silently routing to settings.

The minimum fix would be a UI message when Connect ends up back at the installation settings page rather than completing the OAuth callback — currently it fails silently with no feedback.

```json
    {"id": "slack", "name": "Slack", "status": "not_configured", "expiresAt": null}
  ],
  "activeConnections": 1,
  "expiredConnections": 1
}
```

## Key design points

- JSON output is the canonical machine-readable format
- Fields are stable and documented
- Compatible with `--filter` to query specific services
- No new dependencies - JSON serialization is already in the dependency tree

## Why small

This is purely an output format change. All the data is already collected and displayed - just add a JSON serializer path.

items.title: Feature: Approval Paths — pluggable manual-approval delivery channels (ntfy push)

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
## Problem

Today a `manual_approval` policy rule can only be resolved via the OneCLI SDK long-poll. That works for SDK/CLI users, but on Mac/web (and for out-of-band approval) there's no way to approve/deny from a phone, and the approver runs on the same host the agent controls.

## Proposal

Introduce **Approval Paths** — a set of independently-toggleable delivery channels for manual-approval decisions, designed to extend to N channels:

- **OneCLI SDK** — the existing long-poll, now gated behind an explicit (default-on) flag so it can be turned off.
- **ntfy** — the gateway publishes an Approve/Deny push to a self-hosted [ntfy](https://ntfy.sh) server; tapping a button POSTs to a token-guarded gateway callback that resolves the held request.

Both channels resolve the same in-memory `PendingApproval` store, so any combination can be enabled at once.

### Highlights

- New project-scoped `ApprovalPath` model (purely additive migration).
- Per-channel hold timeout (the held request uses the longest among enabled channels).
- Token-guarded callback routes `POST /v1/approvals/{id}/approve|deny` that are **idempotent and conflict-aware** (same decision → 200, opposite → 410, timed-out/unknown → 408) — important because mobile push clients retry and users double-tap.
- A dashboard connection test that exercises publish → device → callback without an agent, plus a recent-events debug log.
- Optional, default-on confirmation note back to the topic (security signal when someone else resolves a request; also compensates for iOS action buttons giving no inline feedback).

All gateway work lives in the OSS modules. Happy to discuss scope/curation — opening a PR with the implementation to make the discussion concrete.

items.title: Dashboard sidebar shows "User" instead of the signed-in account

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
### Problem

In the dashboard, the lower-left sidebar always renders the signed-in user as
**"User"** with an empty email, even though the account is fully authenticated.

### Root cause

The client AuthProvider (`apps/web/src/lib/auth/auth-provider.tsx`) reads the
session with NextAuth `useSession()`, which expects a `{ user: { id, email } }`
shape. But `/v1/auth/session` is served by the OneCLI API (`packages/api`) and
returns the profile **flat**:

```json
{ "id": "...", "email": "...", "name": "...", "projectId": "...", "organizationId": "..." }
```

So `session.user` is always `undefined`, the provider treats the user as
anonymous, and the sidebar falls back to the literal "User".

The dashboard layout already reads this endpoint correctly via
`apiFetch("/v1/auth/session")` and uses the flat shape — only the auth provider
is out of step.

### Proposal

Read the session in the auth provider the same way the layout does: fetch
`/v1/auth/session` via `apiFetch` and take `id`/`email`/`name` off the response
root. PR ready.

(Related: #362 / PR #380, which fix the NextAuth SessionProvider basePath.)

items.title: container-config returns ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=placeholder instead of CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=placeholder when OAuth token is configured

labels.name: area/gateway
labels.description: Proxy, routing, TLS, DNS, credential injection

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
## Problem

When an Anthropic OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`) is stored as a `type: anthropic` secret, the `/api/container-config` endpoint still returns `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=placeholder` in the `env` block — the same value it returns when no Anthropic secret is configured at all.

The correct placeholder for an OAuth token is `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN=placeholder`, which instructs the Claude SDK to send `Authorization: Bearer placeholder` instead of `x-api-key: placeholder`. The gateway only injects OAuth tokens into the `Authorization` header; it never matches `x-api-key`.

The net result: **OAuth token injection silently never fires** regardless of agent secret mode.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Configure a `type: anthropic` secret with a valid OAuth token (`sk-ant-oat01-...`)
2. Set the agent to `mode: all`
3. Call `GET /api/container-config?agent=default` — observe `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=placeholder` in `env`, no `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`
4. Route a request to `api.anthropic.com` through the proxy with `x-api-key: placeholder` → `credential_not_found`
5. Route the same request with `Authorization: Bearer placeholder` → injection succeeds ✅

The gateway injection itself works correctly (step 5 confirmed). The bug is exclusively in the container-config response.

## Expected Behaviour

When the configured Anthropic secret is an OAuth token, `/api/container-config` should return:

```json
{
  "env": {
    "CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN": "placeholder"
  }
}
```

And **not** `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=placeholder`, or at minimum return both so the SDK can prefer the OAuth path.

## Observed Behaviour

`/api/container-config` always returns `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=placeholder` regardless of whether the configured credential is an API key or an OAuth token. The `warnings` array also reports *"No Anthropic credentials configured"* even when a valid OAuth token is stored — suggesting the validation step itself may be using `x-api-key` to validate OAuth tokens (which would always fail, since OAuth tokens require `Authorization: Bearer`).

## Workaround

In the NanoClaw agent-runner, filter `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` from the subprocess environment when `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN` is present:

```ts
env: Object.fromEntries(Object.entries(process.env).filter(([k]) => k !== 'ANTHROPIC_API_KEY'))
```

This is a client-side patch; the correct fix belongs in `/api/container-config`.

## Environment

- OneCLI Cloud (api.onecli.sh), SDK `@onecli-sh/sdk` v0.5.0
- NanoClaw v2 agent containers
- Claude Code session reference: `b17c8777-4f59-4ae4-b968-c140018a5e35`

items.title: Route Google Workspace Events API through the Google Chat connection
items.body:
## Problem

OneCLI's Google Chat provider injects its OAuth token for `chat.googleapis.com`, but Google Chat event subscriptions are created and renewed through `workspaceevents.googleapis.com`.

As a result, an agent with a connected `google-chat` app can call the Chat API, but requests such as:

```text
GET https://workspaceevents.googleapis.com/v1/subscriptions
```

do not resolve to the Google Chat provider and do not receive the connected user's OAuth token.

The current Google Chat connection already requests the Chat user scopes used by Workspace Events subscriptions. The missing piece is provider routing and permission metadata for the second API host.

## Proposed behavior

Treat `workspaceevents.googleapis.com` as part of the existing `google-chat` provider:

- Add a Bearer-auth host rule using the shared Google refresh configuration.
- Add app-permission entries for the subscription lifecycle:
  - list/get/create/update/delete subscriptions
  - reactivate subscriptions
  - get long-running operations
- Keep the connection and consent flow under the existing Google Chat provider rather than introducing another OAuth connection.

## Acceptance criteria

- `provider_for_host_and_path()` resolves Workspace Events API requests to `google-chat`.
- Gateway injection replaces a placeholder bearer token with the connected Google Chat token for that host.
- Permission definitions cover read-only inspection separately from subscription mutations.
- Gateway and permission tests cover the supported host, paths, and methods.
- Existing `chat.googleapis.com` routing remains unchanged.

items.title: Allow BYOC Google Drive connections to request full Drive access
items.body:
## Problem

The Google Drive provider supports both OneCLI platform credentials and user-supplied OAuth credentials, but both paths use the same fixed `defaultScopes`.

PR #140 deliberately changed Drive from full `drive` access to `drive.readonly` + `drive.file` to match the scopes approved for OneCLI's platform OAuth app. That remains the correct default for platform-managed credentials.

For BYOC connections, however, the customer owns the OAuth app and may have an internal or independently verified app that can request `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive`. OneCLI currently provides no way for that connection to opt into full Drive access.

With the existing scopes, agents can read existing files and manage files created or explicitly opened through the OAuth app, but cannot reliably rename, move, update, delete, or change permissions on arbitrary existing files the user can access.

## Current implementation

`resolveAppCredentials()` already distinguishes `app_config` (BYOC) from `env` (platform credentials), but the OAuth route discards that source and always passes the provider's unconditional `defaultScopes` to `buildAuthUrl()`.

## Proposed behavior

Preserve the current verified scopes for platform credentials:

- `drive.readonly`
- `drive.file`

Allow a BYOC Drive connection to explicitly request full access:

- `drive.readonly`
- `drive`

This could be implemented as source-aware scopes or as user-selectable OAuth scopes constrained by credential source. Full Drive access should not become the platform default, and existing connections should retain their current scopes until explicitly reconnected.

## Acceptance criteria

- Platform-managed Drive connections continue requesting only the currently approved scopes.
- BYOC Drive connections can explicitly opt into `drive`.
- The selected scopes are visible before consent and persisted on the resulting connection.
- Existing restrictive connections do not silently gain broader access.
- Tests cover both `env` and `app_config` credential sources.

## Context

This is the Drive equivalent of the existing-file limitation fixed for Sheets in #319, but Drive cannot use the same unconditional replacement because PR #140 documents the platform verification constraint.

items.title: Feature proposal: per-agent network allow lists (deny-by-default egress control)

labels.name: area/gateway
labels.description: Proxy, routing, TLS, DNS, credential injection

items.body:
## What I'm trying to do

  I run [nanoclaw](https://nanoclaw.dev/), an orchestrator that provisions a lot of OneCLI agents, and  I need to restrict where each agent can talk on the network — per agent, not just per org. My ideal default: an agent reaches Anthropic (for AI) and nothing else, and I explicitly allow any other domains it needs. Some agents I lock down hard, others I allow access to a few sites (some with injected API keys).  Others I leave generally open (also injecting API keys to a few sites). I want to set this at provisioning time via the management API, and manage it from the web UI.

  ## Why the gateway doesn't give me that today

  1. **Deny is tied to credentials.** In `forward.rs` / `websocket.rs`, deny is
     effectively `has_injections && !is_llm_host(host)`, so it only blocks hosts
     the gateway already has credentials for — a "deny" agent can still reach
     `evil.com`. That's the opposite of an allow list.
  2. **Mode is org-only.** `policyMode` lives on `Organization`, so I can't lock
     down one agent and leave another open, and there's no UI for an allow list.

  ## What I built

  Expressed through the existing policy engine and `PolicyRule` storage — not a
  second system. Three per-agent states out of existing machinery:

  | State | Stored as | Behavior |
  |---|---|---|
  | **Locked (default)** | `policyMode = deny`, no extra rules | Only hosts with OneCLI-managed credentials (AI via my LLM key) |
  | **Allow-listed** | `deny` + agent-scoped `Allow` rules | Credentialed hosts + the domains I name |
  | **Open** | `policyMode = allow` | Unlimited |

  - **Data model:** nullable `Agent.policyMode` (`null` = inherit org); effective mode resolved via `COALESCE(a.policy_mode, o.policy_mode)`, no extra query.
  - **Enforcement (the core fix):** dropped the `has_injections` coupling and the `is_llm_host` bypass — `enforce_deny` is now just "is the effective mode `deny`?". Added a **CONNECT-time host gate**: in deny mode, an unmatched host gets a structured **403 on the CONNECT** (no tunnel opened).
  - **Credentials-imply-allow:** in deny mode a host with OneCLI-managed credentials is implicitly allowed, so my AI backend stays reachable with no seeded rule.
  - **Management API:** `PATCH /agents/:id` takes `policyMode: "allow" | "deny" | null` so nanoclaw can set mode at
    provisioning; allow entries reuse the existing `/rules` endpoints. Audited + cache-invalidating.
  - **Web UI:** per-agent mode control (Inherit / Locked / Open) with an allowed-domains editor, a global allow-list section, and `allow` as a first-class rule action.
  - **Blocked-request contract:** the blocked CONNECT returns a recognizable 403 (header + JSON naming host/agent + remediation hint) so nanoclaw's agents get a clear message, not an opaque proxy error.

  Upgrades are safe: existing orgs are pinned to `allow` on migration (no change), new orgs default to `deny`.

  ## How this sits next to #366

  Different layer, and I think both are useful: **#366** scopes what an agent reaches *inside* a connected provider; **mine** is whether it can reach a host *at all*, at CONNECT. One overlap — my branch and #366 both added a
  `session_policy: Option<serde_json::Value>` field in `connect.rs` / `mitm.rs` / `db.rs` (mine for scoped-token refresh, #366's for its request guard). On rebase I'd want these to become one resolved `session_policy` channel feeding both,
  rather than one overwriting the other.

  ## Where I'd like your input

  1. Is deny-by-default per-agent egress something you'd take upstream?
  2. The exact Anthropic hosts the OAuth/token-exchange flow touches, so credentials-imply-allow keeps AI access working.
  3. Should I keep "always log LLM traffic" independently of the `is_llm_host` bypass I removed?
  4. Global allow list at org level (what I did) vs. project?
  5. Preferred shape for the blocked-CONNECT 403, to match existing gateway errors.

  I have a working implementation (gateway + API + web + migration + docs) and can open a PR if you are interested.

## Editorial note

Much of the details of this were written by AI, but I reviewed it and particularly shaped the motivation and the input section.

items.title: Self-hosted multi-user OAuth Problem in 1.35.1: client requests /api/auth/* but server mounts NextAuth at /v1/auth/*
items.body:
## Summary
  
  After enabling Google OAuth multi-user mode on a self-hosted gateway, the dashboard fails to sign in because the client-side React code requests `/api/auth/providers` while the server-side NextAuth handler
  is mounted at `/v1/auth/*`. Result: 404, redirect to `/api/auth/error` (also 404), no path to a working multi-user install. This blocks Projects, blocks the multi-account feature shipped in #187 (only
  exposed via the org API), and effectively makes self-hosted multi-user mode unusable in 1.35.1.
  
  ## Environment
  
  - Gateway image: `ghcr.io/onecli/onecli:1.35.1` (digest `sha256:7339d4490…`)
  - CLI: `onecli` 2.2.4 (macOS arm64)
  - Host: macOS 14, Docker 29.3.1
  - Mode: self-hosted, transitioning from single-user → multi-user
  - Postgres: bundled `postgres:18-alpine`
  
  ## Reproduction 
  
  1. Fresh self-hosted gateway running on `127.0.0.1:10254` with the default `docker-compose.yml`, no `.env`.
  2. In Google Cloud Console: create OAuth 2.0 Client (Web application) with authorized redirect URIs:
     - `http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/callback/google`
     - `http://127.0.0.1:10254/v1/auth/callback/google`
  3. Create `~/.onecli/.env`:
     ``` 
     ONECLI_VERSION=1.35.1
     NEXTAUTH_SECRET=<openssl rand -base64 32>
     ``` 
  4. Create `~/.onecli/docker-compose.override.yml` to inject the Google vars (the bundled compose only maps `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` in its `environment:` block, not `GOOGLE_*`, so this override is also required —
  see "Secondary issue" below):
     ```yaml
     services:
       onecli:
         environment:
           GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID:-}
           GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET: ${GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET:-}
     ```
  5. Add `GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID` and `GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET` to `~/.onecli/.env`.
  6. `docker compose up -d`. Container becomes healthy.
  7. Open `http://localhost:10254/auth/login` in a fresh Chrome incognito window. Click the Google sign-in button.
  
  ## Observed
  
  ```
  GET http://localhost:10254/api/auth/providers
  → 404 Not Found
    {"error":{"message":"Unrecognized request URL (GET: /v1/auth/providers). ...","type":"invalid_request_error"}}
  
  GET http://localhost:10254/api/auth/error
  → 404 Not Found
    (same gateway "Unrecognized request URL" body)
  ```
  
  Browser address bar lands at `http://localhost:10254/api/auth/error` with no `?error=…` query string (because NextAuth never got far enough to attach one — the providers fetch failed first).
  
  Meanwhile, the same endpoints under `/v1/auth/*` work correctly server-side:
  
  ```
  GET http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/providers  → 200
  {"google":{"id":"google","name":"Google","type":"oidc","signinUrl":"http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/signin/google","callbackUrl":"http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/callback/google"}}
  GET http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/csrf       → 200 {"csrfToken":"..."}
  GET http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/session    → 200 (returns {} or session)
  ```
  
  The Next.js routes-manifest inside the container confirms only `/v1/auth/[...nextauth]/route` and `/v1/auth/session/route` are registered — there are no `/api/auth/*` routes.
  
  ## What I tried that didn't help
  
  Setting these in the container env (via the override compose) made the SERVER side report the right URLs (the `signinUrl`/`callbackUrl` in `/v1/auth/providers` updated to the `/v1/auth/...` form), but the
  CLIENT side still requested `/api/auth/providers`:
  
  - `NEXTAUTH_URL=http://localhost:10254/v1/auth`
  - `AUTH_URL=http://localhost:10254/v1/auth`
  - `AUTH_TRUST_HOST=true`
  
  Grepping the built client chunks under `/app/apps/web/.next/static/chunks`:
  - No `SessionProvider` `basePath` prop assignment found
  - No `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` env var for auth basePath defined or referenced
  - Only `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` and three `NEXT_PUBLIC_COGNITO_*` vars exist on the public side
  - The only hardcoded auth path in the built code is `/v1/auth/session` (one occurrence); everything else NextAuth-related is constructed at runtime by the library default

## Impact
  
  - Self-hosted multi-user OAuth is fully blocked in 1.35.1
  - Projects feature inaccessible (gated on multi-user)
  - Multi-account connections (#180 / #187) are gated on the org API which itself is gated on multi-user
  - The 1.35.1 release note "restore default project fallback for self-hosted auth" suggests this area is being actively maintained — this issue is likely a close cousin

items.body:
# Feature Request: GCP / BigQuery authentication support in OneCLI

**Reference:** https://cloud.google.com/bigquery

## Goal

Enable OneCLI to broker auth for the BigQuery REST API (`bigquery.googleapis.com`) so a sandboxed agent can run scheduled, read-only queries without holding a long-lived key.

## Gaps blocking this today

1. The existing Google OAuth apps (Drive, Sheets, Calendar, Docs, etc.) don't include a BigQuery scope, so there's no app to connect.
2. Generic Secrets are static, but BigQuery requires a short-lived OAuth access token that expires hourly — a static bearer stops authenticating within the hour.

## Proposed solutions (either works)

- A **"Google Cloud / BigQuery" OAuth app** with scope `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/bigquery.readonly` (or `cloud-platform.read-only`), **OR**
- A **GCP service-account credential type**: upload a service-account JSON key and have OneCLI mint + refresh short-lived access tokens from it, injecting them as `Authorization: Bearer` on `bigquery.googleapis.com` requests. This matches how most GCP automation authenticates (service accounts rather than user OAuth) and covers read-only analytics/reporting use cases.

## Impact

Without a refreshing GCP token, BigQuery must be queried outside the gateway and results fed in separately — unlike other HTTP APIs OneCLI already brokers cleanly.

items.title: Support self-hosted connectors with user-defined instance URLs

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
## Summary

OneCLI's gateway matches incoming requests to providers using a static host-pattern table compiled into the binary. This works well for SaaS services with fixed hostnames (e.g. `api.github.com`) but prevents supporting self-hosted services whose hostnames are deployment-specific (e.g. `affine.mycompany.com`, `gitea.homelab.local`, a private Jira instance).

Today there is no supported path for a user to connect a self-hosted service unless its hostname is hardcoded in the provider registry.

## Current behaviour

The gateway `HostPattern` enum supports two variants:

- `Exact(&'static str)` — matches a specific hostname
- `Suffix(&'static str)` — matches a hostname suffix (e.g. `*.jfrog.io`)

Both require the hostname to be known at compile time. There is no mechanism for a user to specify "my instance of service X lives at `affine.example.com`" through the connect UI and have the gateway honour it.

## Expected behaviour

Users should be able to:

1. Enter their instance URL in the service connect card (alongside API key / token)
2. Have the gateway automatically route requests to that hostname through the matching connector — no env vars, no config files, no restart required

The credential set (stored per connection) is the right place to record the instance URL, since it is per-user and per-deployment.

## Proposed implementation

### Near-term: `HostPattern::Env(&'static str)`

Add a third variant that reads the target hostname from a named environment variable at match time:

```rust
Env("AFFINE_HOST")  // matches when AFFINE_HOST == request hostname
```

- Zero DB access at match time; env var is read once per request
- Never matches when the var is unset or empty — safe default
- Lets operators configure the hostname at deployment (e.g. in `docker-compose.yml`) without a binary change
- Combined with the existing `credential_host_field` gate (per-connection host check), leakage to wrong tenants is prevented even if the env var changes

### Longer-term: `HostPattern::Credential`

A follow-on variant that matches against the stored `host` credential field of active connections. Eliminates the env var entirely — all configuration flows through the connect card UI. Requires a lightweight secondary lookup path in the gateway resolver.

## Impact

Blocks AFFiNE connector (see companion issue), and will block any future self-hosted connector (Gitea, Forgejo, Nextcloud, self-hosted Jira, etc.).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `HostPattern::Env(var)` variant added to `apps/gateway/src/apps.rs`
- [ ] `HostPattern::Env` matches case-insensitively; never matches when var is unset or empty
- [ ] Existing `credential_host_field` gating continues to work as a per-connection security layer on top
- [ ] Unit tests: unset var → no match, set var → match, case-insensitive match, other hosts → no match
- [ ] Self-hosted connector documentation notes the env var requirement

items.title: Unable to add Agent or Credentials in fresh install
items.body: # Creating an agent fails with 401 "Invalid API key or token" on a fresh self-hosted (local mode) install Just came across this project and wanted to check it out, but had an issue actually creating an agent when running locally. Fresh self-hosted instance, default local mode, and clicking "Create Agent" in the dashboard returns 401 "Invalid API key or token". It turns out the same thing happens for basically every project-scoped action in the dashboard (listing/adding secrets, etc.), so the self-hosted UI is mostly unusable. See the affected-endpoints list below. Version: 1.35.0 (also reproduces on a clean DB). ## Repro Fresh install, nothing custom: ```sh git clone https://github.com/onecli/onecli cd onecli docker compose -f docker/docker-compose.yml up -d ``` No `.env`, no `NEXTAUTH_SECRET`, so it comes up in local mode. The container's `/app/data/runtime-config.json` is `{"authMode":"local","oauthConfigured":false}`, and `GET /v1/auth/session` returns the local admin fine: ```sh curl -s http://localhost:10254/v1/auth/session # {"id":"...","email":"admin@localhost","name":"Admin","projectId":"","organizationId":"..."} ``` But creating an agent (what the dashboard POSTs) 401s: ```sh curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:10254/v1/agents \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ --data-raw '{"name":"test","identifier":"test"}' # {"error":{"message":"Invalid API key or token.","type":"authentication_error"}} # 401 ``` Add the `x-project-id` header (value from `/v1/auth/session` above) and the exact same request works: ```sh curl -s -w '\n%{http_code}\n' -X POST http://localhost:10254/v1/agents \ -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \ -H 'x-project-id: ' \ --data-raw '{"name":"test","identifier":"test"}' # {"id":"...","name":"test","identifier":"test","createdAt":"..."} # 201 ``` So the only difference between 401 and 201 is the `x-project-id` header, which the dashboard never sends in local mode. ## Affected endpoints This is not specific to creating agents. Every route that goes through `authMiddleware` 401s the same way without `x-project-id`. Confirmed by hand: - `POST /v1/agents` (create agent) - `GET /v1/agents` (list agents) - `GET /v1/secrets` (list secrets / the LLM connections page) - `POST /v1/secrets` (add a credential) Looking at `packages/api/src/app.ts`, the only routes that do NOT use `authMiddleware` are `/v1/health` and `/v1/auth/session`. Everything else does: `agents`, `secrets`, `rules`, `user`, `apps`, `gateway`, `gateway-url`, `container-config`, `counts`, `skill`, `credential-stubs`. So in practice the whole project-scoped dashboard is unusable in local mode, not just agent creation. I only reproduced the four above by hand, but the rest go through the same middleware, so there are likely more. ## Cause The project-scoped routes require `x-project-id`, but the self-hosted middleware never sets it. - `packages/api/src/middleware/auth/resolve.ts:40-41` returns null when the header is absent: ```ts const headerProjectId = request.headers.get("x-project-id"); if (!headerProjectId) return null; ``` - `packages/api/src/middleware/auth/session.ts:26` then bails, so `authMiddleware` returns 401: ```ts if (!projectId && requireProject) return null; ``` - `apps/web/src/proxy.ts` is what would inject the header, but it only does so for cloud. The non-cloud branch returns early before the injection block: ```ts // proxy.ts if (!IS_CLOUD) { // ...scope-strip + redirect... return NextResponse.next(); // returns here, no x-project-id set } // header injection (requestHeaders.set("x-project-id", projectId)) only runs below, cloud-only ``` The matcher also excludes `v1` (`apps/web/src/proxy.ts:82`), so the API requests are not rewritten by middleware at all. Net: in local/self-hosted mode nothing supplies `x-project-id`, but `authMiddleware` requires it for project-scoped routes, so the dashboard can create nothing. ## Notes - `GET /v1/auth/session` works because it does not go through `authMiddleware` (it calls the session provider directly), which is why login looks fine but every project-scoped action fails. That makes it look like an auth/login problem when it is actually a missing header. - The README does not mention the `.env` file at all, so the first guess is that `.env`/`AUTH_MODE` setup is the problem. It is not: the entrypoint already derives `authMode: "local"` when `NEXTAUTH_SECRET` is empty, with or without an `.env`. Worth a line in the README either way. - Also, changing Agents in the "Getting Started" model doesn't appear to do anything currently, if you switch to "Autonomous Agents" and then close the modal, next time you open it, it has returned to "Coding Agents". ## Workaround Until fixed, project-scoped calls work if you pass `x-project-id` from `/v1/auth/session`. Not usable from the dashboard UI without an extension that injects the header. ## Suggested fix In local mode, resolve the user's default project when `x-project-id` is absent (the local admin has exactly one), rather than returning null. Either in `resolveProjectId` (fall back to the default project for the local user) or by having the self-hosted path in `proxy.ts` inject `x-project-id` the way the cloud path does.

items.title: oauth2.googleapis.com/token misrouted to vertex-ai for non-Vertex Google providers

labels.name: has-pr
labels.description: A community PR exists for this issue

items.body:
**Title:** oauth2.googleapis.com/token misrouted to vertex-ai for non-Vertex Google providers

---

## Summary

OneCLI's gateway routes every `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` request to the `vertex-ai` provider, regardless of which Google product originated the refresh. When `vertex-ai` is unconfigured (the common case for users who only use Gmail/Drive/Calendar/etc), the gateway returns `401 {"error":"app_not_connected","provider":"vertex-ai"}` for every refresh attempt. Any MCP server built on `google-auth-library` then surfaces `Invalid Credentials` to the agent, breaking every write operation that hits an access-token refresh.

This contradicts the `add-gcal-tool` skill docs in [`nanocoai/nanoclaw`](https://github.com/nanocoai/nanoclaw/blob/main/.claude/skills/add-gcal-tool/SKILL.md), which explicitly state: *"the OneCLI gateway intercepts outbound calls to `calendar.googleapis.com` / `oauth2.googleapis.com` and swaps the bearer for the real OAuth token from its vault."*

## Repro

1. Connect `gmail` (or `google-drive`, `google-calendar`, etc) via BYOC OAuth in OneCLI dashboard. Do **not** connect `vertex-ai`.
2. From inside any OneCLI-proxied container, attempt an OAuth refresh:
   ```bash
   curl -sS -X POST \
     -d 'client_id=onecli-managed&client_secret=onecli-managed&refresh_token=onecli-managed&grant_type=refresh_token' \
     https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token
   ```
3. Returns `401`:
   ```json
   {
     "error": "app_not_connected",
     "provider": "vertex-ai",
     "hostname": "auth.openai.com",
     "message": "Vertex AI is not connected in OneCLI..."
   }
   ```

(`hostname` field oddly says `auth.openai.com` — possibly a separate templating bug in the error message.)

## Resource-endpoint behavior (works as expected)

Same container, same stub token, against a Google resource endpoint:
```bash
curl -sS -H "Authorization: Bearer onecli-managed" https://www.googleapis.com/drive/v3/about?fields=user
```
Returns `200` with the real user's Drive metadata. So the gateway's per-provider token injection works for resource calls — only the refresh-endpoint dispatch is broken.

## Root cause (per PR #224 review)

PR #224 ("feat: add Vertex AI integration with ADC import and token endpoint interception") added the `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` host rule to the `vertex-ai` app definition in `apps.rs`. A reviewer noted at the time:

> The `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` host rule on the Vertex AI provider exists to feed data to the interceptor, not for actual proxying. A comment on that rule in `apps.rs` explaining this coupling would help future readers.

The interceptor was intended to be provider-discriminated, but in practice the host rule is the only registration of `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` anywhere in the app definitions. Every Google product's refresh request matches it, and the dispatcher treats all matches as Vertex AI calls.

## Impact

Every MCP server that wraps `google-auth-library` and tries to refresh an expired token via the OneCLI proxy gets a confusing 401 attributing the failure to Vertex AI. Affected community servers include (non-exhaustive):

- `@gongrzhe/server-gmail-autoauth-mcp`
- `@cocal/google-calendar-mcp`
- `@piotr-agier/google-drive-mcp`
- `@scottie-will/google-tasks-mcp`
- `google-workspace-mcp` (covers Docs/Sheets/Slides/Forms)

Users see "Invalid Credentials" on the first refresh attempt and have no visible path to a fix beyond skipping the MCP layer and calling Google APIs with raw `curl` (which works because the resource-endpoint injection is unaffected).

## Suggested fix

Dispatch the `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` interception based on something other than hostname alone:

- The stub `client_id` / `refresh_token` (currently always `onecli-managed`, but the gateway could namespace stubs per provider on issue, e.g. `onecli-managed:gmail`).
- A request-tagged provider context attached when the proxy first sees a resource call from that connection.
- Or: split the rule so each Google provider's app definition carries its own `oauth2.googleapis.com/token` registration, and the dispatcher picks the connected provider whose recent resource calls match the calling container's session.

Documenting the coupling in `apps.rs` (per the original review comment) would also catch this for future contributors.

## Env

- OneCLI v1.23.0
- macOS 25.4.0 (darwin/aarch64), Docker 29.4.3
- Container runtime: NanoClaw v2.0.64 agent containers (Linux/aarch64)

items.title: Sub-agents inherit "All credentials" instead of parent agent's selective scope
items.body:
## Summary

When an agent with Selective credential access spawns a sub-agent, the sub-agent does not inherit the parent's restricted scope. Instead it appears to get the "All credentials" default, allowing it to access secrets the parent agent was explicitly restricted from.

## Environment

- Open-source OneCLI (not the managed version at app.onecli.sh)
- Used in combination with nanoclaw for agent orchestration

## What happened

I run several developer agents (mei, diego, rahul, sarah), each with their own dedicated GitHub PAT, isolated so each agent only has access to its own Anthropic key and its own PAT. The original agents were manually configured to Selective credential access.

One agent (mei) was assigned a task and spun up a sub-agent (x-builder) to do the work. The resulting PR was authored by a different agent (diego), because x-builder had access to the full set of secrets and happened to use diego's GitHub PAT rather than mei's.

In other words, the sub-agent was able to reach credentials that its parent (mei) was explicitly scoped away from.

## Expected behavior

A sub-agent should inherit the credential scope of its parent agent. If mei is restricted to Selective access (its own Anthropic key + its own PAT), any sub-agent mei spawns should be limited to that same scope, not granted "All credentials."

An agent should not be able to escalate beyond its own Selective secret scope by spawning a sub-agent.

## Actual behavior

Sub-agents are created with "All credentials" access regardless of the parent agent's configured scope, matching the default applied to new agents created manually via the dashboard.

## Additional notes

- New agents created manually through the dashboard also default to "All credentials" rather than Selective. This can be changed manually, but there is no opportunity to do so when an agent (rather than a human) creates the new agent.
- I've since locked down the secrets in OneCLI and also restricted the "Default Agent" (which had access to all secrets) down to Anthropic only.

items.title: Google Sheets permission prevents editing existing files
items.body:
Hello, when setting up oncecli with my local Nanoclaw installation, I discovered a problem where I could not have my agent update an existing Google spreadsheet that I've had around for years. 

Looks like the [authentication](https://github.com/onecli/onecli/blob/main/packages/api/src/apps/google-sheets.ts#L30-L34) defined for sheets is `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file`. It seems like this allows creating NEW spreadsheets and writing to them, but not for editing existing ones. 

The correct permissions look to be:

* Read only: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly`
* Read and Write: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets`

Or if you want to be more granular with onecli's permissions for agents:

* Read only: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets.readonly`
* Read and Write EXISTING sheets: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/spreadsheets`
* R+W Sheets the App / Agent created: `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/drive.file`

## Workaround

To workaround this, I installed the [Webhooks for Sheets extension](https://workspace.google.com/marketplace/app/webhooks_for_sheets/860288437469). This exposes an API to append new rows to a sheet.
